items.headline: Wohngeld — Reform ("Neuordnung") im Kabinett: Leistungen sinken
items.what_changed: Cabinet passed a draft law to "simplify and further develop" the Wohngeldgesetz. The Wohngeld formula coefficient **C is being adjusted downward**, which *reduces* payouts; Freibeträge change, notably for people with care needs (Pflegebedarf). Framed as budget stabilisation + bureaucracy reduction.
items.effective: Draft stage (Referentenentwurf → Kabinett). Not yet in force — watch the Bundestag reading.
items.who_affected: All ~1.9m Wohngeld households, especially low-income renters and care-dependent claimants near the cut-off.
items.citizen_tip: If you are close to the eligibility edge, **apply now** under current rules — entitlement is assessed at application date.

items.headline: Wohngeld — Haushalt 2026: Ansatz erhöht (+€150.13m)
items.what_changed: Bundestag budget committee raised the 2026 Wohngeld budget line by **€150.13m** above the government draft (Einzelplan 25).
items.who_affected: Signals capacity for continued payouts despite the cut-oriented reform — no direct change to individual entitlement.

items.headline: Bürgergeld → "Neue Grundsicherung": harsher sanctions from 1 July 2026
items.what_changed: Bürgergeld is renamed and restructured into the **neue Grundsicherung** (SGB II). Key points:
items.who_affected: ~5.5 million recipients. Highest risk: people in high-rent cities (stricter KdU checks) and anyone who misses mail/appointments.
items.citizen_tip: Always answer Jobcenter letters and cancel appointments in writing with a reason — the new rules punish no-shows fastest.

items.headline: Elterngeld — Prien draft: 14 → 12 months, 3 "Vätermonate", higher min/max
items.effective: Not yet law; targeted for ~2027 births. Current births still under 14-month rules.
items.who_affected: ~1.61m Elterngeld recipients/yr (1.19m women, 417k men). Couples splitting leave unequally lose the most.

items.headline: Kindergeld — €259/month since 01.01.2026, automatic payment planned
items.what_changed: Kindergeld rose to **€259 per child/month** on **1 Jan 2026** (from €255). Coalition plans a two-stage rise toward **~€272**, plus **abolition of the application** (automatic payment via tax-ID linkage).
items.effective: €259 in force now; automation and further increases still planned.
items.who_affected: All families with children — the automation step mainly helps families who currently never apply.
